Power 
 Station

Technical 
 Procedure

Equipment:Electric Governor 
 for Hydraulic Turbines
Introduction

This document outlines the 
testing procedure P1, which must be performed on an annually bases as indicated 
by Y1 in the title block

The present electric - hydraulic 
governor system represents the latest development in a continuing program - 
designed to provide the best equipment available for hydraulic turbine speed 
control - the hydraulic turbine governor is on longer just a speed response 
control of the turbine

The first draft initiated 
and 
tested by eng. Khaled Saeed Mohamed, accepted by eng. Nagy Nageeb Saleh: general director, 
approved by eng. Mohamed Abd Elbasat head sector of Aswan Dam 
Hydraulic power station and certified by eng. Kamel Raghib Hakem: HPGC quality 
control general director and MPIS 
coordinator.
Safety Precautions

A work permit must be issued and the maintenance staff should carry the suitable ID safety 
 category.

Maintenance staff should be qualified trained or directly supervised by 
 some one who is
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area is required.

Wear the personal safety and healthy protective equipment as safety shoes, 
 helmet ... etc
Switch off the DC power supply before inserting or withdrawing the relay.

 8 Volt (RMS)

Electric frequency counter to accurately set the signal generator output to 
 the desired frequency
Multi-range DC voltmeter

A good oscilloscope and digital voltmeter are very handly to have, although 
 not always necessary

Preparation

Turn off the governor 
power supply

Pull all modules in all 
racks

Turn on the governor power 
supply transfer switch to the test position
Check the main supply (AC-DC)

Check the main supply (AC-DC)

sections.text: Calibration Procedure

Set the cam to the 16 M 
index mark, this is the position for minimum net head as from the 3D cam

Loosen clamps on the head 
/ gate feedback potentiometer (65 MHP) and adjust so that the slider voltage is 
0 VDC from terminals 4 (signal) to terminal 12 (common) on DZ
(Note: if 0 Vdc cannot be attained, set as close as possible). Tighten clamps. 
This will set the offset of the isolation amplifier (DZ) to 0 Vdc so the gain 
can be properly calibrated

Adjust the potentiometer 
(P4) for 0Vdc from terminal 6 (out put) to terminal 7 (common) on DZ
This will set the offset of the isolation amplifier to 0 V so the gain can be 
properly calibrated

Set the cam to the 30 M 
index mark

Adjust the gain 
potentiometer (P1) of DZ for a reading of -9.307 Vdc from terminal 6 (out put) 
to terminal 7 (common). This will set the proper gain for the potentiometer 
feedback

Reset the cam to 16 M 
index mark

Again loosen the clamps on 
the head / gate feedback potentiometer. Adjust so that the slider voltage is -1 
Vdc. Tighten clamps. This is to insure that the potentiometer will not overrun 
its travel

Adjust the offset 
potentiometer (P4) of DZ to read -0.303 Vdc from terminal 6 (output) to terminal 
7 (common)

Set the cam at the 
30 M index mark and check for -9.61 Vdc from terminal 6 (output) to terminal 7 
(common) of DZ
